아름다워요 (ㅂ irregular). Strong and a bit poetic: for scenery, or a very sincere compliment. Bold.
사랑스러워요 (ㅂ irregular). Tender, more for couples. Warm.
매력 있어요 = you're attractive. Safe and common. Mild to warm.
매력적이에요. A notch more serious than 매력 있어요. Warm.
똑똑해요. To anyone. Mild. To an elder, praise their knowledge instead.
착해요. Big compliment from a partner's family; to equals or juniors only. Mild.
to be affectionate; sweet and caring
다정해요. A top quality in a partner. Warm.
미소가 예뻐요. A little literary; speech also uses 웃는 모습. Mild.
눈이 예뻐요. Praising eyes is safe and common. (눈 also = snow.) Mild to warm.
A Korean favourite: eyes curving into crescents when you smile. Warm.
보조개가 귀여워요. A classic Korean compliment. Mild.
목소리가 좋아요. Safe, very common, especially on the phone. Mild.
웃음이 많아요 = you laugh a lot (a good thing). Mild.
분위기 있어요 = you have a certain charm. Very Korean compliment. Warm.
제 스타일이에요 = you're my type. Mild alone; warm in that phrase.
성격 좋아요 is high praise. Mild.
센스 있어요 = you've got taste / you're thoughtful. Mild.
Koreans ask 이상형이 뭐예요? on first dates and in interviews. Mild as a question.
첫인상이 좋았어요 = I liked you from the start. Warm.
Slang, from 훈훈한 남자. For women: 훈녀. Mild, friendly.
Slang: 심장이 쿵. 심쿵했어요 = you made my heart skip. Warm, playful.
To a woman you know. 오늘따라 = today especially. Warm.
Right after learning a name. Mild, sweet.
You must hear that you're pretty a lot
Indirect and smooth. To a woman. Warm.
To someone you know well. 짓 = little actions. Warm, playful.
Polite -시-; to a man you don't know well. Mild to warm.
After seeing photos first (dating app, a friend's phone). Warm.

Classic office or café crush line. Warm.
To someone your age or younger. Mild.
Safe on a date or between friends. Mild to warm.
Safe on a first meeting. Mild.

Often on the phone or after karaoke. Mild.
I wanted to hear your voice
Why you called. To someone you're dating. Warm to bold.
You have a certain charm about you
A refined compliment to men or women. Warm.
Bold and playful. Usually after a few dates.
I liked my first impression of you
And you have a great personality too
도 = on top of being good-looking. Warm.
Have you eaten? (I care about you)
Korean's indirect "I'm thinking of you". Polite form of the casual 밥 먹었어? Mild.
Often polite filler; when meant, it opens a date. Ask "when?" to show you mean it. Mild.
Easy opener after class or work. Mild.
Is it OK if I contact you?
Polite way to ask for KakaoTalk. Mild.
At the end of a first meeting. Warm.
Want to come up for some ramyeon? (joke line)
From the film One Fine Spring Day (2001), where the line is 라면 먹을래요?; this meme version means an invitation inside. Joke only, never a real move.
Playful deflection, shy but not a no. Casual and friendly.
Teasing deflection; smiling = interested, flat = not. Mild.
A warm yes to an invitation.
Thanks for the thought, but I'm fine
Kind, clear no. Works for a drink or a number.
Clear no; nobody will push after this.
You're a lovely person, but I'd like to stay friends
Gentle no to someone you know. 분 keeps it respectful.
I'm not looking to date right now
Compliments: -네요 = noticing out loud. Say it to the host or cook during the meal.
솜씨 = skill with your hands. Polite -시-; fine to elders.
Asking for the recipe is praise in itself.
For any skill. To elders, praise with -시- and no grading words.
To colleagues and friends. To a boss: 좋은 생각이신 것 같아요.
To equals or juniors. It sounds odd said to a much older person.
You have a great sense of humor
배려 = thinking of others. Highly valued.
Always busy and on time. Different from 열심히 하시네요 (works hard at it).
A very common, friendly compliment in Korea, to men and women alike.
You look so young for your age
A favorite compliment, especially to people over 30.
Literally "your impression is good". Said on first meeting.
Said on a first visit, often with a gift (휴지, fruit).
Parents will usually deflect: 아니에요, 말썽꾸러기예요.
A compliment to the parents too. Very welcome.
What learners hear right after 한국어 잘하시네요.
Usually follows the compliment; itself a compliment.
To a friend or junior. To an elder it sounds like grading.
The polite way to praise a boss: you report your experience, you don't grade them.
The safest praise for a senior, teacher or boss.
Thank you for all your hard work
Praises effort. Fine among colleagues; some seniors find 수고 from a junior presumptuous, so to a boss 감사합니다 is safer.
The first reflex after any compliment: deflect, even if you're pleased.
Oh no, I still have a long way to go
The standard modest reply, especially about your Korean.
Don't mention it; you're too kind
Polite and a little formal. To elders and at work.
Literally "that's too much praise". Polite, a bit formal.
Accepting warmly. More common among younger people.
Thanks for seeing it that way
The host's answer to praise for food or a gift.
Turns the praise back onto the other person. Warm and humble.

desc.Top nouns: The most-used Korean nouns the course doesn't teach yet, most frequent first.
desc.Top verbs: Action verbs in dictionary form; the note gives the 해요 form and flags irregular verbs.
desc.Top adjectives: Descriptive verbs (Korean adjectives are verbs): the 해요 form and the form before a noun.
desc.Top adverbs: Time, degree, frequency and manner words: very, already, often, why, how.
desc.Top pronouns: I, you, this one, who, nobody, and why names and titles usually replace 'you'.
desc.Top particles: Korean's answer to prepositions: the particles beyond the nine in the Particles deck.
desc.Top connectors: Joining endings (-고, -지만, -아서, -(으)면 …) shown on a verb, plus linking words not in Connectors.
desc.Top interjections: What Koreans really exclaim: wow, ouch, oops, phew, ta-da, and who says each one.
desc.Top words: This / that / which before a noun, number forms, days and times, and ways to say yes and no.
desc.Top counters: Counters missing from the Counters deck: cars, portions, rolls, slices, minutes, months.
desc.Flirting words: The words Koreans flirt with, phrases built from them, and kind ways to say yes or no.
desc.Compliments: Everyday praise for food, work, homes and children, and the modest ways to answer it.
